title: Launchpad visual system for first-run quickstart: modular hero, progressive steps, and screenshot pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a cohesive visual system for the Quickstart landing page that we internally call the 'Launchpad'. The Launchpad should introduce new users to Redwood Inference with a compact hero, horizontally-scrolling modular tiles for common starter flows, and progressive step components that surface only the next-most-important task. This ticket scopes art direction, final Figma comps for desktop/tablet/phone, screenshot capture standards, and handoff assets for front-end implementation.
goals: Reduce time-to-first-success for new signups by clarifying the minimal steps to call the API
Provide a flexible hero that can accommodate 3 marketing variants and A/B copy tests
Ship a screenshot capture pipeline and naming convention so product screenshots are reproducible for releases
Ensure visuals are accessible and responsive across 320–1440px widths
deliverables: Hero art system: primary illustration + headline variants + CTAs (3 variants for A/B)
Modular Launchpad tiles: 4 tile types (API quickstart, SDK snippet, Console walkthrough, Example app)
Progressive steps component: collapsed/expanded states, microcopy, success badges
Screenshot capture doc: scripts, viewport presets, anonymization checklist
Handoff package: Figma files, export-ready PNG/SVG/JPEG assets, CSS token suggestions
assets_needed: Hero illustration in 3 aspect ratios: 16:9, 4:3, 3:2 (SVG + 2 raster sizes)
Tile icons: 32/48/64px SVGs with 1x/2x PNG exports
Sample console screenshots: desktop 1366x768, tablet 820x1180, phone 390x844
Microinteraction frames for Lottie export (30fps, 4–6s loop max)
acceptance_criteria: Figma comps reviewed and signed off by PM and Engineering
Exported screenshot set follows naming convention and includes placeholder anonymization
Responsive styles documented and tokenized (spacing, colors, typography)
Three hero copy/art variants ready for A/B test and flagged in Launch roadmap
Design-to-dev handoff artifacts uploaded to the /design/handoff folder with clear acceptance checklist
screenshot_pipeline_notes: Use headless chrome script (repo above) with /stable viewport presets to ensure consistent renders
Run anonymization step that strips API keys and workspace names, replaced with consistent placeholders
Include a 'golden' token set for colors/typography to prevent visual drift across releases
Store exported assets under /assets/quickstart/<release>/ with semantic filenames: hero-variantA_1366x768.png
responsive_considerations: Mobile-first grid: 4 columns at >= 1024px, 2 columns at 600–1023px, 1 column <600px
Hero illustration should gracefully crop to the right on narrow viewports; avoid essential copy overlaying art
Tile interactions convert from hover to tap affordances; ensure 48px touch targets
Progressive steps should be keyboard-navigable and support reduced-motion preferences
engineering_notes: Frontend should accept hero variant flag via query param for A/B testing (query param: launchpad_variant)
Provide CSS token suggestions (color tokens, spacing scale, breakpoints) in the handoff doc
Coordinate with ENG infra to include screenshot route that returns sanitized images for marketing use
Prefer SVG for icons with a PNG fallback for legacy email templates
risks_and_tradeoffs: Using vector-first hero improves scale but increases Figma complexity and export QA time
Progressive disclosure reduces cognitive load but may hide advanced options for power users — include an explicit 'show all' affordance
Aggressive image optimization could reduce fidelity for small text in screenshots; keep a high-res master for marketing

notes_for_PM: Recommend running inclusion test for the three hero variants on a small cohort of new signups (2 weeks) to measure time-to-first-success and CTA conversion. Track metrics: signup->first-API-call and signup->first-embed-creation.
final_comment: Keep the Launchpad visual language modular so Marketing can reuse tiles for other campaigns. If we go wide with illustrations, create a compact icon set for low-bandwidth contexts.
